title: Task scheduler as a Node.js service
idea: As a Node.js service, the scheduler keeps tasks in a PostgreSQL table: an API inserts them idempotently, and workers claim due rows with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`.
points: The table replaces the in-memory heap; an index serves the due-task query.
POST takes an `Idempotency-Key`, so a retried request never creates a second task.
Each claim locks one due row and skips rows other workers hold.
A failure writes a later `run_at`, which is backoff that survives a restart.

steps.caption: The client posts a task with an `Idempotency-Key`. The API inserts one row.
The client times out and retries with the same key. The unique key returns the same task.
More tasks arrive. Both workers ask for the best due row at the same moment.
Worker 1 locks charge. Worker 2 skips that locked row and takes flaky.
Flaky fails. Worker 2 writes it back as SCHEDULED with a run time 30 seconds later.
Worker 1 claims report and finishes it. Only flaky waits, due again at 10:00:30.
At 10:01 flaky is past its new run time (10:00:30). Its second attempt succeeds and the row is done.

code.title: Task API
code.caption: Create, read and cancel tasks: 201, an idempotent 200 replay, 400, 404 and 409.

walk.text: The table enforces status values, priority range and one task per key.
Insert, or do nothing if this key was already used.
Cancel only a SCHEDULED row, in one conditional update.
A replay returns the stored task instead of creating another.
No row changed: 404 if missing, else 409 because it moved on.
Zod checks the body: name, ISO run time, priority 0 to 9.
Errors map to HTTP codes in one place.

code.title: Workers with SKIP LOCKED
code.caption: Two workers drain due tasks in parallel at three moments. Each claim is unique, and failures back off.

walk.text: The task table, plus a partial index of only SCHEDULED rows in claim order.
Flaky fails its first attempt; broken always fails.
Lock the best due row, skip locked ones, mark it RUNNING.
Succeed, give up at the limit, or reschedule with doubled backoff.
Each worker claims until no due row is left.
Run two workers at 10:00, 10:01 and 10:05; count claims.

pitfalls: Follow-up: a crashed worker leaves rows RUNNING; add a lease expiry that returns them.
Follow-up: a reused Idempotency-Key with a new body should get 409, not the old task.
Follow-up: for many workers, claim small batches and keep the partial index.

quiz.q: What does worker.mjs print for the 10:00 round?
quiz.why: Five rows are due at 10:00; later is not. SKIP LOCKED gives each row to one worker, and retries land 30 seconds later.

takeaway: Store tasks in a table; claim due rows with SKIP LOCKED.

starters: How do I recover tasks stuck in RUNNING after a worker crash?
Why not use LISTEN and NOTIFY instead of polling for due tasks?
How would I guarantee a job runs exactly once, not at least once?
